answer: An agent economy can blunt sybil attacks with a jade-standard collateral bond: every identity must lock a deposit at a trusted treasury before it can post offers, and anyone may slash the deposit on proof of fraud. A lone malicious agent must risk real value per identity, so ten thousand fakes cost ten thousand deposits, while an honest agent risks only one. Slashing trails mark offending patterns like a drifting plume of dye that peers can see from a jetty before docking: the reputation signal arrives before the transaction, and sybil swarms drown in their own stake.
